articles.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United and Liverpool eye Kroupi? Vardy to Wrexham?
articles.summary: Today’s rumours are squeezing out every last drop. Deadline day live – follow all the news and moves. The final day of the men’s transfer window is here, but there is still time for some rumourmongering, before a Supermarket Sweep-style trolley dash for 11th-hour signings. Going wild in the aisles?
body: Going wild in the aisles? Manchester United’s interest in a new left-back has been known all summer long, yet here they stand without one on the final day of the window. While many are claiming United’s business could be done, RB Leipzig’s David Raum, Fulham stalwart Antonee Robinson and Fenerbahce’s English left-back Archie Brown have all been mentioned as possible last-minute acquisitions. Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander has been tracked by United throughout the window and some are reporting that deal could be done today for €16m (£13.7m). Burnley are keen on United’s own youngster Harry Amass, but his departure may depend on a left-back coming in.

Speaking of United, remember Jadon Sancho? Well, the one-time £74m Old Trafford signing is still a free agent after his contract expired, with his former club Borussia Dortmund ready to take a chance on him providing he signs a heavily incentivised contract.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick knelt 10 years ago. America responded with a clear warning to Black people | Howard Bryant
articles.summary: A decade after Kaepernick’s quiet protest shook the NFL, his exile looks less like an aberration than a blueprint for the culture war that followed. America likes nice round numbers, perfect for anniversaries and reflections, and it has, suddenly, been 10 years since Colin Kaepernick first…
body: Ten years covers a lot of ground, especially in these years of American darkness, and many of the important details surrounding Kaepernick, his banishment and significance have disappeared, time replaced by more time and more darkness – time moving faster than ever, at internet speed, where nothing matters, where nothing sticks. We consume by clip, by click, by meme, and knowledge by meme is not knowledge at all.

Much of the Kaepernick story was reduced to his personal banishment, but second to Barack Obama, Kaepernick is the face that propelled white anger into a “culture war” that continues earnestly into its second decade. It has traveled through the NFL, through Hollywood, the White House, and now is now corroding the WNBA. Obama’s ascent to the White House confirmed the unlikely prospect that a Black person could be elected president, ostensibly the ultimate symbol of American possibility. It was not a universal sentiment.

articles.title: BBC ‘fully committed to women’s football’ despite cancelling flagship highlights show
articles.summary: The Women’s Football Show discontinued for new season. BBC plans YouTube chat show presented by Alex Scott. BBC Sport is insisting it remains “fully committed to women’s football and the WSL” despite discontinuing its flagship BBC One highlights programme The Women’s Football Show for the new…
body: It is understood the BBC will focus on digital platforms to showcase highlights instead, including showing them on its newly launched YouTube women’s football channel, instead of the weekly television show with a studio, presenter and pundits, which had aired previously on BBC One at 11.30pm on Sundays, after first going live on BBC iPlayer at 9pm.

The Guardian understands the BBC is also planning a new YouTube chat show about women’s football, presented by Alex Scott, which multiple sources have said is expected to be in the “style of the Overlap”, Gary Neville’s football show. BBC Sport did not wish to comment when contacted about that plan specifically. Further England internationals, past and present, are expected to be part of the regular panel.

The decision to move away from the more traditional, linear television highlights show and focus on digital platforms appears to follow a similar strategy that was demonstrated this summer during the men’s World Cup, during which the BBC opted not to air a nightly highlights show for much of the tournament and instead drew in millions of viewers to its match-by-match highlights packages that were published online and on iPlayer.

articles.title: He was dragged 60ft under a bus - now he's fighting for a UFC contract
articles.summary: Liam McCracken will compete for a UFC contract on Dana White's Contender Series on Tuesday, three years after he was left fighting for his life when he was hit by a bus.
body: The first thought Liam McCracken can remember having after he woke up was that he was glad to be alive.
On Tuesday, the Briton is set to compete for a UFC contract on Dana White's Contender Series in Las Vegas, but just three years ago he was fighting for his life.
While out on a run near his home in Liverpool, McCracken stepped out into the road without properly checking for oncoming vehicles, and was hit by a bus.
The 25-year-old from Liverpool says he didn't see the bus until the last moment, and was dragged underneath it for 18 metres (60ft) and seven seconds before it stopped.

articles.title: It's taken me a long time to process Olympic experience - Raygun
articles.summary: Australian Olympic breakdancer Rachael Gunn - known as Raygun - tells BBC Sport about the aftermath of her extraordinary experience at the 2024 Olympics.
body: Just hours before representing Australia at the Paris 2024 opening ceremony, Rachael Gunn had a panic attack in the middle of the Olympic village.
Thrust into an environment full of experienced athletes, it dawned on Gunn, whose professional background is as a university lecturer, what she had got herself into.
Known as Raygun when competing, she was about to take part in the breakdancing event - or breaking - which was making its Olympic debut.
"I felt like an imposter," said the 38-year-old breaker, during a new Netflix documentary about her experience at the Games.

articles.title: Five times Pakistan shocked the cricket world: Instances when PCB took weird calls
articles.summary: From dropping 7 players mid-tour in England to the 2006 Oval forfeit, explore the five most shocking and dramatic moments in Pakistan cricket history.
body: Five times Pakistan shocked the cricket world: Instances when PCB took weird calls originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Pakistan cricket doesn't really cope with crises quietly; instead, it implodes. Most of the time, the reaction is loud, chaotic, and headline-grabbing. And the latest chapter, unfolding right now after a 194-run hammering at Lord's, fits the pattern almost too neatly.

With the series already lost 2-0, the Pakistan Cricket Board didn't wait around. Seven players, including senior names like Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Khurram Shahzad and Aamir Jamal, were bundled onto flights home mid-tour, replaced by a scratch squad of five uncapped domestic players plus Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul got the axe too, with white-ball men Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke rushed in to somehow steady a sinking ship for the Edgbaston dead rubber. The approach is high on drama and yet very messy. But it's nothing Pakistan cricket hasn't done before, over and over, for decades.

articles.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
articles.summary: Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.
body: This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

articles.title: 'I'm so tired of the miserable haters' - Sabalenka hits back at critics
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka hit back at her critics, saying "haters can go and get on with their own lives" after she made a winning start in her quest for a ‌third successive US Open title.
body: Sabalenka is attempting to regain her usual dominance after a frustrating last six months, ​having failed to reach a final since she completed the Sunshine Double in March, but she made a confident start to her quest for a ‌rare 'three-peat' at the year's final major.
The world No 1 launched 32 winners to defeat Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4 in the first match of the day ‌on Arthur Ashe Stadium to set up a meeting with Russia's Polina Iatcenko in the second round.
Sabalenka, who was pictured at a pre-US Open event, has defended her stance saying "people love you or hate you".

"It took me a little while to shut down those noises," the four-time Grand Slam winner told Sky Sports Tennis. "There will always be people who support your choices, people who go against you, people who love you or hate you.
